reasoning_traces.think:
The dualGNN framework integrates two distinct yet complementary loss components—energy score (ES) and variogram score (VS)—to jointly optimize both marginal calibration and spatial dependence in ensemble post-processing. ES evaluates forecast accuracy via integrated squared error, while VS captures spatial variability through pairwise differences in feature space. By combining these in a weighted sum, L = w1·ES + w2·VS, the model learns to balance local reliability with global coherence. This composite loss enables one-step multivariate calibration, bypassing the need for sequential steps like ECC or Schaake shuffle. The choice of weights (e.g., 0.9 ES / 0.1 VS for irradiance) reflects empirical trade-offs between calibration fidelity and spatial realism. The use of GraphSAGE ensures that spatial relationships among nodes (e.g., stadiums) are encoded via adjacency matrices derived from similarity measures rather than geographic proximity. This allows for more accurate propagation of uncertainty across geographically distant but climatically similar regions. The model’s architecture supports end-to-end training with early stopping and validation splits, ensuring robustness against overfitting. In GSE applications, this translates to generating coherent joint weather ensembles across multiple venues in a single forward pass, crucial for real-time game-day forecasting.
